review_scope: Manual reading of experiment/result sections in all 29 supplied PDFs, plus representative rendered table/reference pages. PDF page numbers are one-based file pages, not printed page numbers. Observations describe the supplied versions, not verified final venue requirements. Unknown does not mean absent.

profiles.experiment_order: Implementation -> indoor/outdoor tracking -> separate prediction and trajectory-planner comparisons (pp.5-6).
baseline_groups: Prediction module: Chen et al. [10]; planner module: Jeon et al. [9] (p.6).
metrics: Future-position distance error under low/mid/high observation noise (p.6).
Front-end, back-end, total latency and effective tracking-time ratio rt; effective distance threshold explicitly defined (p.6).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: Prediction shares polynomial/history/horizon parameters; >15000 predictions per noise condition. Planner receives the same ground-truth future target motion, separating planner quality from differing predictors; 200 missions per target-speed scenario (p.6).
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Vary observation Gaussian noise and target speed; indoor clutter and dense forest test re-location/tracking behavior. A distinct module ablation was not identified in pp.5-6.
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: Broad-FOV three-camera detection; approximately 20 ms system total and 15 Hz replanning; indoor/outdoor maps paired with real scene images (p.5). CPU model not resolved from these pages.
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Two small tables answer two separate module questions; scenario-grouped planner rows keep runtime and task metric adjacent. Fig.9 explains trajectory differences rather than repeating the table (p.6).
profiles.transfer_boundary: An end-to-end system claim also needs end-to-end tests: supplying ground-truth target futures isolates the planner and cannot establish realistic prediction robustness. Do not treat lower acceleration alone as a measured energy result.
profiles.citation_profile: Bracket-number citations are placed beside borrowed corridor/optimization/detection methods and baseline names. Reference list has numbered hanging entries with quoted titles and italic venues, but full names and initials are mixed (p.7).

profiles.experiment_order: Formation-method benchmark -> implementation -> two real flights -> larger irregular-formation simulation (pp.5-6).
baseline_groups: Zhou [23] and Turpin [29], with obstacle avoidance adapted for Turpin (p.5).
metrics: Success rate, similarity-aligned position error edist, graph similarity error esim (p.5).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: Seven drones, three obstacle densities, fixed speed cap; competing parameters tuned for performance. Sim(3) alignment removes allowed rotation/scale differences from the position-error score (p.5). Trial count not located in these pages.
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Density sweep and regular/irregular, 2D/3D formation scenarios; corridor passage tests compression and rotation. Distinct ablation not located in pp.5-6.
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: Xavier NX onboard, RealSense D435, trajectory broadcast; i9-9900K simulation computer. Seven-drone planar and four-drone tetrahedron flights; ten-drone heart-shaped simulation (p.6).
profiles.presentation_inheritance: One scenario-grouped numeric table plus upper/lower baseline/ours snapshots carrying formation-error annotations, followed by real scene/map panels (pp.5-6).
profiles.transfer_boundary: Related precursor of R04; do not count both as independent corroboration. Do not reuse the score normalization without checking which transformations the new claim permits.
profiles.citation_profile: Bracket citations identify baseline rows and measurement inspiration (p.5); numbered IEEE-like entries at p.7.

profiles.experiment_order: Speed/density benchmark -> component replacement ablation -> desktop/onboard runtime breakdown -> real flight profiles -> limitation (pp.6-8).
baseline_groups: Learning [7], FastPlanner [3], Reactive [9]; Gao corridor method [16] is the modular ablation base (p.6).
metrics: Success rate vs forward speed and forest density (p.6).
Mapping/planning mean and standard deviation, total latency (p.7).
Flight duration, length, mean/max speed and dynamic limits (p.7).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: Reproduced unavailable benchmark environment; baseline results partly taken from [7], thrust limits differ and are disclosed. Ten runs per speed/density; success includes velocity, acceleration and collision constraints (p.6).
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Factorial-style replacements: Gao, Gao+MINCO, Gao+MINCO+RHC, own front+MINCO, full. Adds extreme density. Reused-corridor failure limitation is discussed (pp.6-8).
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: i7-10700 desktop and i7-10710U onboard runtime; real LiDAR quadrotor, twelve attempted forest flights with eleven trajectory profiles and one disclosed controller failure (p.7).
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Four side-by-side success-vs-speed panels isolate density; runtime table groups mapping/planning rows. Real trajectory composite is registered across independent flights, and its caption explains that processing (p.7).
profiles.transfer_boundary: Label reproduced, reported and directly rerun baselines separately. Runtime hardware conditions and differing dynamics budgets must accompany comparisons. Do not hide the failed twelfth flight when selecting eleven successful trajectories.
profiles.citation_profile: Bracket numeric in text, baseline labels and captions. Bibliography on p.8 uses full author names and period-separated titles without the conventional quoted-title IEEE entry shape; imitate only if chosen target permits it.

profiles.experiment_order: Define fair formation metrics/parameters -> adaptability -> predictability -> reorganization -> global agreement/path finding -> decoupling efficiency -> real flights and complementary simulations (pp.11-16).
baseline_groups: Position-, displacement-, distance-based formation definitions (p.12).
VRB and spatial-only vs spatial-temporal optimization (pp.12-13).
With/without ALAS; Alonso-Mora global planning; previous coupled formulation [4] (pp.14-15).
metrics: Normalized edist/esim; success, path length; desired/minimum formation scale; runtime vs robot count (pp.11-15).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: Four formation shapes x four rotation/scale-change scenarios x twenty runs; same navigation setup with tuned competing parameters. Global planners tested twenty times; excludes ALAS when isolating coupled/decoupled optimization (pp.12-15).
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Initial assignment disorder, a constrained hole, tiny obstacles, shape switching and larger robot counts each correspond to a named method property (pp.13-16).
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: i7-12700 benchmarks; distributed onboard system with up to sixteen real drones, tetrahedron corridor flight and 3D formation transformation. Runtime curve extends beyond physical swarm size (pp.12,15-16).
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Full-width table groups formation types in columns and scenario/variant in rows; best cells bold. Smaller tables compare method properties. Event-labelled photographs/RViz panels share an error-vs-time plot (pp.13-16).
profiles.transfer_boundary: Borrow the property-to-test correspondence, not the number of tests. R02 is related work in the same research line. Large simulated scaling does not imply equally large real flights.
profiles.citation_profile: Baseline citations sit in table row labels and comparison setup; numbered IEEE-like references start at p.18. Match named competing mechanisms to exact references rather than attaching a bundle to a generic criticism.

profiles.experiment_order: Real platform/protocol -> planning success vs catching success -> dynamics case traces -> capability/runtime comparison -> controlled simulated target families and RL algorithms (pp.7-9).
baseline_groups: Motion Primitive Planner MPP [1] for real catching; PPO/SAC/TQC for high-level decisions in controlled simulations (pp.7,9).
metrics: Planning success, catching success and optimal time ratio OTR, whose lower direction is explicitly defined (p.7).
Body rate, thrust, velocity and jerk feasibility; computing time (pp.8-9).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: Same computer for MPP; fifty real throws per planner. One thousand simulated tests per target-motion scenario; simulation removes prediction/sensing/control/delay errors to isolate decision planning (pp.7,9).
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: One to six targets with parabola/harmonic/triangle/hexagon motion; consecutive/multiple catches; compare planned actuator limits on the same recorded throwing case (pp.8-9).
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: i5-1135G7 onboard; Vicon gym and custom net quadrotor; captions specify measured vs desired traces and net/robot dimensions (pp.7-8).
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Two levels of success must remain separate. A large composite figure relates catching sequence, 3D positions, hardware dimensions and dynamic traces; a compact table separates algorithm capability from numeric outcomes (pp.7-9).
profiles.transfer_boundary: A high-level time-selection policy is not a motor policy. OTR is undefined for methods without a comparable decision output; use N/A with reason, never an invented zero.
profiles.citation_profile: Bracket numeric identifies algorithm and controller sources alongside claims; tables carry MPP [1] and policy-family names. References begin on p.10.

profiles.experiment_order: Controlled sharp-turn benchmark -> sudden-deceleration benchmark -> real T-intersection demonstration and comparison (pp.6-7).
baseline_groups: Ji tracker [5], with position/yaw broadcast in simulation and target-position broadcast for real baseline to mitigate localization effects (p.7).
metrics: Occlusion percentage/time and failure rate across target speeds; tracker-relative target-position heatmap and horizontal distance during deceleration (p.7).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: Identical initial tracker positions, identical target paths and tracker limits; three target-speed levels and approximately fifty random sharp turns (p.7).
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Turn and deceleration scenes test different intention consequences: visibility preservation and safe relative distance. Separate intention-component ablation not identified in pp.6-7.
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: i7-12700F simulation; D435, monocular target camera, Pix32v6 Mini, NUC-12WSKi7 real platform (pp.6-7).
profiles.presentation_inheritance: A staged turn panel and entire-route occlusion trace sit together; target-relative heatmap is paired with one event's distance-time curve. Real camera and RViz views show the same turn (pp.6-7).
profiles.transfer_boundary: A selected turn explains behavior, while the multi-turn statistic supports frequency. Keep broadcast/ideal target inputs explicit and do not interpret the local case as a broad robustness rate.
profiles.citation_profile: Numbered baseline citation is bound to the named method; sensing/state-estimator references are placed at implementation use. Numeric IEEE-like refs at p.8.

profiles.experiment_order: Simulation setup/metrics -> density x number of blind UGVs -> four removal variants -> real platform and uncertainty/collision-time traces (pp.5-6).
baseline_groups: Self-perception UGV reference with onboard LiDAR/SLAM (p.5).
Without RPE measurement, uncertainty propagation, scheduling, or collision time windows (p.6).
metrics: UGV reach/wait time and path length; UAV path length; maximum wait in ablation; state uncertainty and predicted collision time (pp.5-6).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: Sparse/dense maps and 1/3/5/7 UGV configurations; measured wheel noise seeds simulation parameters. Removal study fixes dense map and five UGVs. Number of independent repeats not located here (pp.5-6).
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Without localization or uncertainty handling, failures are reported rather than forced numeric completion metrics; greedy scheduling and no-time-window variants isolate coordination (p.6).
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: MARSIM/numerical UGV simulation; Intel NUC i7-1165G7, CREPES relative pose and Mid-360 sensing; one UAV and three UGVs in physical arena (p.6).
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Main table groups density/UGV count; ablation table uses dash for failed runs with failure explanation in text. Real event trace links support visits to uncertainty drops and collision-time increases (p.6).
profiles.transfer_boundary: Self-perception hardware is a reference ceiling with different sensing, not an equal-information algorithm baseline. Separate group-size bottlenecks from universal navigation claims.
profiles.citation_profile: Numeric citations identify common EGO-Swarm/MARSIM/OR-Tools modules and RPE device. Numbered IEEE-like references at p.7.

profiles.experiment_order: Noise-free offset tolerance/optimality -> joint offset x noise error sweep -> real trajectories, cost/pose/time error and runtime (pp.5-6).
baseline_groups: Wang [6] without time-offset estimation; proposed non-iterative NTO and iterative ITO variants (p.5).
metrics: Offset estimation error, cost, rank; relative-pose errors; real translation/rotation error, estimated offset, runtime (pp.5-6).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: One hundred Monte Carlo trials per offset; 11000 samples for offset/noise grid. Removes anonymity consideration from baseline for fair comparison; zero offset output used explicitly for baseline's undefined estimator (p.5).
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Offset grows beyond the approximation regime; error heatmaps disclose failure regions. Five real trajectory patterns with 1 s imposed offset and motion-capture ground truth (pp.5-6).
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: MATLAB/CVX single-core i5-9400F; quadrotors with infrared cameras/LED arrays for real inter-robot bearings (pp.5-6).
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Three-method heatmaps share noise/offset axes and color scale; real per-run results keep pose, clock and latency columns together; trajectories explain registration failures (p.6).
profiles.transfer_boundary: Optimization minimum does not automatically imply best state accuracy under noise; this caveat is explicit on p.6. Background synchronization runtime cannot be claimed as control-loop latency.
profiles.citation_profile: Bracket numeric identifies baseline adaptations, synthetic trajectory construction and solver. IEEE-like numeric references at p.7.

profiles.experiment_order: Main article: multi-vehicle planning comparison and scaling -> real car-team aircraft catching/transport (pp.6-8). Supplement begins at PDF p.9; do not treat all twenty-three PDF pages as main text.
baseline_groups: FOTP [5], MNHP [8], DMPC [7], SCP [22], CL-CBS [3] (p.6).
metrics: Success, computation time, mean/longest travel time, average total distance and acceleration cost, global/decentralized capability distinctions (p.6).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: One hundred random obstacle cases; varied agent counts. Same Hybrid A* initial guess supplied for applicable methods, with further details routed to supplement (p.6).
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Agent-count scaling separates runtime growth from trajectory quality. Real rescue net tests size/topology constraints; expected fall location and time are assumed known (pp.7-8).
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: i7-12700/32 GB benchmark; three car-like robots and central eighth-generation Intel platform described in source, trajectories tracked by MPC. CPU naming in p.8 is internally unusual; retain as source wording rather than silently resolving model (pp.6,8).
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Wide grouped table has agent-count rows within each method and separate capability columns; sequential rescue composite pairs physical snapshots and global path (pp.6-7).
profiles.transfer_boundary: Known fall state is not a demonstrated perception pipeline. Missing smoothness/acceleration outputs for search-only baselines are N/A. Do not infer main-article size from combined-file page count.
profiles.citation_profile: Bracket numeric for baseline labels, model and controller sources; main numbered bibliography p.8, supplement bibliography p.23 is separate.

profiles.experiment_order: Implementation and measured computation model -> baseline definitions -> single-robot -> multi-robot -> CARLA challenge -> real testbed (pp.6-10).
baseline_groups: PF, CAMPC, RDA, PDD-Edge, PDD-Local, EDF with the same PDD planner attached for fair comparison (p.7).
metrics: Navigation time, success, execution latency vs horizon/obstacle count, planner switching and controls; per-robot/total completion time under compute budgets (pp.6-10).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: Fifty trials for single-robot aggregate; separate communication/computation latencies and explicit switching thresholds; compare shared planners while varying placement or scheduler (p.7).
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Crossroad/dense traffic, changing radio region, blocked corridor, moving server and tighter total compute threshold isolate the need for switching/resource assignment (pp.7-10).
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: Ryzen 9 5900X and RTX3090 Ti workstation; measured planner timings on Ryzen and Orin NX. LIMO robots with Jetson Nano, Diablo edge server with Orin NX (p.6).
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Map/radio-map pair -> aligned controls/switching traces -> per-robot outcome table. Baseline footnotes disclose modifications and exact success definition (pp.7-10).
profiles.transfer_boundary: Scheduling/communication setup is part of the causal comparison. Do not cite solver speed as end-to-end navigation speed; source prose/table reduction percentages show discrepancies, so recompute from raw values before reuse.
profiles.citation_profile: Bracket numeric includes theorem-specific pinpoint citation, model implementation references and baseline footnote; IEEE-like numbered bibliography p.11.

profiles.experiment_order: General tracking benchmark -> visibility case -> perching benchmark -> perching visibility removal -> real system -> tracking -> high-speed/night/attitude perching (pp.11-17).
baseline_groups: Tracking: Jeon [20], Elastic-Tracker [21], Fast-Tracker [18]. Perching: Paneque [41], Mao [40], previous planner [10]; commercial DJI Active Tracking for real tracking comparison (pp.11,13-14,17).
metrics: Projected closest-occluder distance Docc, FoV/too-near/occlusion failures, path/optimization latency; observable distance/duration; terminal perching error and dynamics (pp.11-17).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: Same target trajectory and parameter set for tracking. Perching compares rest-to-rest targets, aligns thrust bounds, replaces baseline perception cost for task compatibility; initialization/sampling alternatives disclosed for Mao (pp.11,13-14). Aggregate trial count not located for general tracking.
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Obstacle density, 3D vs pseudo-3D occlusion, terminal pitch and visibility term; real target speed, night light and road roughness distinguish perception/control challenges (pp.12-17).
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: i5-9400F/GTX2060 simulation; onboard DJI MAVIC3 embedded implementation with 20 Hz replanning; full-size SUV target and front/down cameras (pp.11,16).
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Heatmap + violin distribution + failure-count panel; case trajectories aligned with occlusion-highlighted time plots; w/wo visibility table grouped by terminal angle; photos/map/error plot of the same event (pp.12-17).
profiles.transfer_boundary: Docc is excluded for Fast-Tracker when its failure type makes that criterion meaningless. Capability table checks are not measured rates. Visibility under one sensing geometry must not be assumed for every camera arrangement.
profiles.citation_profile: Bracket numeric baseline IDs are carried into tables/plots; Eq. and algorithm citations identify reused constructions. Numbered references begin at p.18.

profiles.experiment_order: Simulation with constant-speed backbone and reward-stage removals -> separate EVA comparison/perception case -> wall-hidden obstacle and dense real clutter (pp.6-7).
baseline_groups: EGO backbone at constant speed caps; policies trained using only either reward stage; EVA-planner [20] as handcrafted adaptation baseline (pp.6-7).
metrics: Full-track success rate and mean successful-trial traversal speed; trajectory velocity colors explain where adaptation occurs (p.6).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: Fifty trials per statistical setup in an unseen evaluation environment; thirty trials in separate EVA speed comparison. Shared backbone parameters aligned; EVA excluded from Fig.6 aggregate with an explicit task-feasibility reason (p.6).
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Two reward stages, partially hidden pillar, changing FoV/latency and dense/large obstacles test perception-aware speed decisions (pp.6-7).
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: Micro drone, D430 and Orin NX; indoor motion capture and outdoor VIO estimates (p.7).
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Use speed-success frontier to show adaptation relative to constant-cap backbone, with training variants on the same coordinate system. Corresponding planned/executed trajectories show controller gap (pp.6-7).
profiles.transfer_boundary: Average speed conditions on successful trials and must be paired with success. This is an outer-loop policy modifying planner speed, not direct control RL. Excluding a failed baseline requires disclosure and a separate capability account.
profiles.citation_profile: RA-L preprint accepted header is visible on p.6. Numeric brackets identify the common backbone and EVA; numbered references p.8.

profiles.experiment_order: Candidate graph-quality scoring metrics -> connection-rate x robot-count trade-off -> sparse-graph baselines -> recovery -> coplanarity ablation (pp.5-7).
baseline_groups: Min-Cond, Max-logDet, Max-MinEigenValue, Max-Trace (p.5).
Random, nearest-neighbor, own method without base-set optimization, complete graph (p.6).
metrics: Normalized formation distortion, relative error vs complete graph, compute time, recovery time and explicit convergence threshold (pp.5-7).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: Shared formation-planning problem; shapes and robot counts varied; twenty randomly regenerated maps per setting, eighty runs for sparse-graph benchmark. Recovery isolates formation from obstacle avoidance (pp.5-7).
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Connection-rate/scale sweeps expose efficiency-error trade-off; with/without optimized base set and coplanar/noncoplanar base vertices diagnose rigidity (pp.6-7).
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: C++ on i7-8700K/32 GB; experiment evidence reviewed here consists of simulations. No physical-flight result identified in experiment pp.5-7.
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Paired runtime/error columns per shape; shaded acceptable trade-off interval; error boxplot; recovery sequence with runtime to its left and recovery time to its right (pp.5-7).
profiles.transfer_boundary: Complete graph is a quality reference as well as a compute baseline. The recommended connection interval and hand-selected trade-off exponents belong to these settings, not a universal swarm rule.
profiles.citation_profile: Numeric citations attach candidate metrics to their source methods and benchmarks to graph roles. IEEE-like numbered refs p.8.

profiles.experiment_order: Planner benchmark/density and scale -> cable-vector ablation -> real platform -> controller mass/agility/compensation/uncertainty tests -> narrow-space and replanning system missions (pp.12-17).
baseline_groups: Wahba kinodynamic planner [26] based on FCL/Crocoddyl (p.13).
With/without cable vector constraints; reference cable force vs INDI force compensation (pp.14,16).
metrics: Planning success/length and runtime vs aerial-robot count; payload mass error; RMSE/MAXE, thrust/RPM/dynamic limits and replanning time (pp.12-17).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: Same dynamic bounds, thirty-six target directions per density; mass estimated ten times for five payloads; five executions per agile/compensation/uncertainty trajectory (pp.13-17).
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Removing vector constraint reveals unwanted topology/local optimum; payload mass varied and intentionally perturbed +/-10/20/30%; object type induces swing; consecutive/emergent replanning tests responsiveness (pp.14-17).
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: C++11 i5-10300H without hardware acceleration; three 320 g aerial robots with Orin NX, motion capture/IMU and broadcast trajectories (pp.13-14).
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Separate planner evidence from controller and system evidence. Tables group payload mass/perturbation and error values; trajectory photos, RViz correspondence and multi-axis measured/reference states form evidence composites (pp.15-17).
profiles.transfer_boundary: A dynamics-coupled payload method needs load/control tests, not only planner success. Simulation scaling does not prove many-drone load handling. Uncertainty range and payload units must remain explicit.
profiles.citation_profile: Bracket numeric credits dynamic models, solvers, planning/controller baselines; parameter table precedes tests; IEEE-like reference block begins p.17.

profiles.experiment_order: Representation/training resource comparison -> speed x density/obstacle-size benchmark -> thin-obstacle and forest real flights -> sensing/training limitations (pp.5-7).
baseline_groups: Occupancy input with 2D/3D CNN vs proposed representation; training environment/mini-batch variations (p.5).
Fast-Planner, EGO-Planner, EGO-Planner v2 (p.6).
metrics: Undiscounted training return, success vs speed and scene, path distance; resource limits explain learning feasibility (pp.5-7).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: Fifty trials per speed in unseen maps; FoV and sensing frequency aligned. Representation comparison explicitly tracks batch/environment counts and memory constraints (pp.5-6).
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Density and obstacle size change independently; thin wires and wind/out-of-range observations in real scenes. LiDAR invalid returns and overly greedy large-obstacle behavior are acknowledged limitations (pp.6-7).
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: i9-14900K and source-labelled 4090 GPU for training; Mid-360/PX4 and Orin NX inference; body-rate response delay is an implementation consideration (p.5).
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Training curve reports data-collection and batch budget; three success-vs-speed panels share method colors; example paths and real close-up obstacle snapshots explain sensing mechanism (pp.5-7).
profiles.transfer_boundary: Representation advantage is coupled to batch/memory budget in this comparison. Separate resource-matched and best-feasible configurations when the new claim demands them. No universal thin-obstacle safety follows from selected flights.
profiles.citation_profile: Numeric citations connect common planner families, state estimator and training implementation; limitations credit comparable sensing work. Refs start p.7.

profiles.experiment_order: Mode transition/trajectory tracking -> continuous attitude tracking -> inclined gap -> curtain operation -> tilted-hover watering application (pp.6-7).
baseline_groups: Within-platform fully-actuated/underactuated modes and step-like/smooth attitude commands; no like-for-like competing-system statistical benchmark located in pp.6-7.
metrics: Position RMSE and attitude RMSE; attitude limits, velocity/acceleration budgets and physical gap/workspace dimensions (pp.6-7).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: NOKOV motion capture for poses; distinct mode limits explicitly stated. Number of independent repeats not resolved from these pages.
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Continuous attitude sinusoid/holds, narrow inclined passage and deformable curtain contact each expose a hardware-specific affordance (p.7).
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: Real fully-actuated coaxial platform; 25 cm diameter and 18 cm minimum width are linked to passage capability. CPU/runtime not identified in pp.6-7.
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Hardware capability manuscript uses a few carefully chosen physical tasks with measured tracking curves, rather than forcing a generic algorithm-baseline matrix (pp.6-7).
profiles.transfer_boundary: Different speed limits across modes are not a controlled superiority comparison. Manually sent position/attitude commands in gap experiment do not establish autonomous scene planning.
profiles.citation_profile: Numeric citations credit attitude/flatness construction; hardware URLs occur in footnotes. Numbered IEEE-like refs p.8.

profiles.experiment_order: Four architectural scenarios -> cross-plane continuity/orientation removal -> representation capability and numeric benchmarks -> tracked-robot stair flight-equivalent deployment (pp.5-6).
baseline_groups: Wang [15], Xu [16], Yang [18] in capability comparison; directly executable 3D comparison narrowed to compatible methods (p.6).
metrics: Trajectory length; path-search/optimization time; map storage size; velocity/continuity and orientation constraints (pp.5-6).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: Same multilayer task; map data standardized to 32-bit floats and redundant ceiling/gradient data omitted for representation comparison. Statistical repeat count not identified in pp.5-6.
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Noisy planes, obstacle platform, multilayer routes and building stairs; orientation constraint removed for a stairs-risk comparison (p.5).
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: CubeTrack with variable-geometry tracks, FAST-LIO2 localization and NUC13; nine-segment non-Manhattan stair environment plus blocked doorway (p.6).
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Environment point clouds -> extracted planes/graph -> ESDF/trajectory arranged as corresponding rows; Boolean capability table is separate from numeric outcome table (pp.5-6).
profiles.transfer_boundary: Representation compression needs equivalent stored content/precision. Boolean ability claims cannot be ranked as statistical planning performance. Robot flipper execution is specific to this platform.
profiles.citation_profile: Bracket numeric baseline labels in prose and tables; localization/robot sources cited at deployment. Numeric references p.7.

profiles.experiment_order: Dataset/setup -> single-robot BA -> multi-robot localization -> map geometry -> loop recall/outlier rejection -> module ablations -> session scaling -> runtime/memory (pp.9-15).
baseline_groups: Module BA: BALM2/HBA; full systems: DCL-SLAM/LAMM; loop rejection: PCM/GNC; FPGO, FPGO+BA, full; full global BA for resource comparison (pp.9-15).
metrics: z-drift/z-RMSE and MME for no-ground-truth single-robot cases; ATE RMSE, AWD/CD/SCS/MME, plane thickness/planarity; loop precision/recall/F1; merge success/runtime/memory (pp.9-15).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: Public S3E/GEODE/MARS-LVIG/R3LIVE plus self-collected data; same raw odometry for BA. Loop methods receive same candidates and parameter sweeps; best-F1 and precision-constrained operating points separated. Loop labels use full-system optimized trajectories as proxy, not independent ground truth (pp.9,13).
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Recalling loops, FPGO/BA/LPGO sequence, coarse/fine geometry, 5/10/20 sessions, runtime vs loop density and OOM handling expose different claim mechanisms (pp.13-15).
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: C++/ROS and real/public sensor datasets; detailed runtime/memory comparisons at p.15. Hardware model not resolved in the reviewed setup; source datasets are not evidence of a new live multi-robot deployment.
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Setup tables list environment/session/trajectory/sensor. Numeric metric headers show units and direction; best cells bold. Global maps plus same-region crops and paired trajectory/error panels connect geometric quality to aggregate scores (pp.9-15).
profiles.transfer_boundary: Do not conflate no-ground-truth proxies with true accuracy. Session splitting is not necessarily simultaneous multi-robot operation. Retain loop-label circularity caveat and fair resource adaptation when interpreting gains.
profiles.citation_profile: Dataset, baseline, MapEval metric definitions and loop-detector citations are at their first operational use. Numeric entries begin p.17.

profiles.experiment_order: Platform -> shape-adaptive vs fixed-size simulation -> morphing traversal -> grasp/transport -> adaptive-controller comparison (pp.5-7).
baseline_groups: Fixed maximum/minimum-size planning [17]; previous controller [6] for same figure-eight deformation task (pp.6-7).
metrics: Position/radius control-effort components, time/total cost, source-defined SORR, model-derived energy; tracking RMSE and external force traces (pp.5-7).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: Hundreds of planning runs averaged; common cluttered narrow-gap environment. Controller uses same figure-eight reference with 1.5 m/s maximum speed (pp.6-7). Exact simulation count not resolved.
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Fixed extreme shapes isolate passability/energy trade-off; grasped body geometry and payload disturbance extend motion/control test (pp.6-7).
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: i7-10700 simulation; radar environmental map and motion-capture/IMU state fusion; morphing quadrotor grasps/transports a physical object through a narrow cross gap (pp.5-7).
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Cost-component table complements matched trajectory renderings; real photo/morphing/map panels paired with position/error/force traces. Controller comparison is a separate evidence question (pp.6-7).
profiles.transfer_boundary: Energy is calculated from a cited power model, not automatically a battery measurement. Cost terms from the objective are not independent metrics unless justified. Keep morphing and grasping evidence distinguished.
profiles.citation_profile: Bracket numeric with comma-separated pairs credits constraints, compensation and energy model; refs at p.8.

profiles.experiment_order: Training-strategy removal/replacement -> static waypoint planning baseline -> moving-waypoint speed stress -> static/dynamic real gates (pp.6-7).
baseline_groups: Sparse reward SP and shaped reward RS vs progressive reset/training; optimization-based aerobatic method [5] in a deliberately static compatible test (p.6).
metrics: Training reward; flight time; aerobatic point position/attitude error; baseline tracking mean/max error; success vs waypoint speed; response/planning latency (pp.6-7).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: Twenty common initial-point sets for static benchmark; fifty trials per moving-waypoint speed; evaluate beyond training motion range (pp.6-7).
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Power loop, barrel roll and split-S; high motion speeds distinguish curriculum effects and reactive control. Direct control has no separate trajectory tracking stage, so tracking metric N/A is intentional (pp.6-7).
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: Real mocap/IMU fused state and tracked moving gates; policy thrust/bodyrate bounds disclosed. CPU for latency measurement not identified in reviewed pp.6-7.
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Training curves beside maneuver trajectories; small table isolates task-point errors from trajectory-tracker errors. Dynamic-speed table is separate, with real static/dynamic gate sequences (pp.6-7).
profiles.transfer_boundary: 0.3 ms policy response and 1.5 s global trajectory optimization cover different operations, so scope timings explicitly. Source Table II labels attitude error as % while prose uses degrees: correct units in new work.
profiles.citation_profile: Bracket numeric identifies aerobatic maneuvers/baseline; quoted baseline ID in table. Numbered IEEE-like refs p.8.

profiles.experiment_order: Number-change scalability -> fixed-number narrow-gap baseline comparison -> simultaneous narrow-space/number-change simulation -> real join/leave -> point-cloud communication test (pp.6-10).
baseline_groups: SF [34], SF-ALAS [11], VRB [21] with swarm-number changes disabled for direct benchmark (pp.8-9).
metrics: Partition/assignment compute time, formation error, collision-free success and traversal time vs gap width, communication mean/std vs point count (pp.6,8-9).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: Same environments/initial formations/dynamic constraints; fifty repetitions per gap. Twenty PAAS runs stated, but table caption calls maximum while prose calls average: statistic is unresolved and should not be silently standardized (pp.6,9).
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Agent join/leave, shape types, up to one hundred simulated agents and narrowing gaps; real few-drone number changes; point broadcast resource curve (pp.6-9).
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: i7-8700K/32 GB simulation; real KAKUTE H7 Mini/Mid360/Orin NX platform. Two-drone point-cloud transmission tested twenty times per size, with mean/max/min delays, supporting 2000 points/message under a 5 Hz budget (p.10). Total system bandwidth is not established by this pairwise test.
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Paired success/time columns repeated under each width; capability baseline table precedes numeric result table; event snapshots aligned with formation-error curves (pp.8-9).
profiles.transfer_boundary: Disabling number changes makes the narrow-gap test fair but does not compare number adaptation. Distinguish maximum from mean compute time; one-shot point-cloud delay does not establish full-network scalability.
profiles.citation_profile: Bracket numeric separates comparative method definitions and inherited formation-error metric; refs begin p.10.

profiles.experiment_order: CARLA qualitative/quantitative end-to-end comparison -> tuning ablation/sensitivity -> real-dataset motion prediction -> embedded resource scaling -> failure-mode caveat (pp.5-7).
baseline_groups: End-to-end: MPC-D-CBF, RDA, OBCA and DT-MPC-disabled variant. Tracking module: KF, KNet, D-KF vs D-KNet (pp.5-6).
metrics: Average/max acceleration, jerk, solver iteration time, passing time/rate; horizon-averaged dB-NMSE mean/std; hardware execution frequency/CPU/memory (pp.5-7).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: Same horizon/time step; one hundred repetitions per obstacle setting and tuning setting; AevaScenes split of eighty training/twenty evaluation sequences; ground-truth boxes used for Doppler point grouping (p.5).
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Obstacle counts, tuning coefficients, tracking frequencies/horizons and highway/city scenes; bounding-box under-segmentation reveals end-to-end failure path (pp.5-7).
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: Orin NX 16 GB embedded prediction benchmark, approximately 107 MB GPU memory; real dataset plus simulation, not an evidenced real dynamic robot navigation trial in pp.5-7.
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Metric rows repeated within obstacle-count blocks; light cell tint marks leading values. Dataset table groups horizon/scenario and frequency with mean +/-std. Qualitative sequence shows predictions and control behavior at matching timestamps (pp.5-7).
profiles.transfer_boundary: Oracle boxes limit full-stack perception claims. Module inference frequency differs from full MPC iteration latency. Hardware tests and recorded datasets must not be labelled live real navigation.
profiles.citation_profile: RA-L accepted preprint header observed p.6. Numeric baseline IDs embedded in column names and captions; named benchmark/dataset citations bind the protocol. Refs p.8.

profiles.experiment_order: Privileged-critic/observation ablation -> domain feature alignment -> real sim-to-real variants -> matched simulated/real trials -> continual reshuffled scenes and illumination stress (pp.5-7).
baseline_groups: No privileged depth, depth actor, RGB actor/privileged critic; baseline, DY, DY+DR, DY+DA and full DR+DA+DY (pp.5,7).
metrics: Training reward; GSI and domain-classification accuracy; simulated/real task success; capability checklist is qualitative (pp.5-7).
profiles.controls_and_sampling: Dynamics randomization remains a shared transfer foundation for relevant variants. Ten test trajectories per simulated/real set; single continuous real flight with obstacle reconfiguration prevents simple scene memorization (pp.5,7).
profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Visual DR vs adversarial DA, held-out augmented styles, sensor/dynamics noise; lighting shifts and moving foliage reveal transfer limits (pp.5-7).
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: Training approximately two days on L40; Orin NX ~2 ms inference; real optical-flow/IMU EKF state estimates (p.5).
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Domain feature rows share baseline/DR/DA/full order; GSI and accuracy quantify the t-SNE picture. Boolean transfer table is paired with actual task success and real round-trip trajectories (pp.6-7).
profiles.transfer_boundary: t-SNE mixing or lower domain-classifier accuracy is not task success. Capability ticks are not numerical transfer rates. Privileged critic depth exists during training, not monocular deployment.
profiles.citation_profile: Numeric citations at GSI, visual augmentation and dynamics randomization definitions; IEEE-like refs p.8.

profiles.experiment_order: Simulation platform/implementation -> hierarchical-decision ablation -> capability/platform comparison -> real unknown-space navigation and extended graph tasks (pp.6-8).

profiles.mechanism_and_stress_tests: Hierarchical decision removal tests long-horizon search; real multi-room semantic exploration; known-space navigation and scene-description capabilities are separate demonstrations (pp.7-8).
profiles.compute_and_physical_evidence: i7-10875H/RTX2060 simulated platform; Orin NX 16 GB, Mid-360, D455 real UAV. Qwen-3 API reasoning is external; other computations local (pp.6-7).
profiles.presentation_inheritance: Environment layout/task trajectory figure -> SPL ablation plot -> property/hardware table -> real scene/resource figure. Hardware placement is part of presentation (pp.6-8).
profiles.transfer_boundary: Do not call the entire stack onboard when the LLM API is external. Platform/frequency rows are heterogeneous literature properties, not equal-condition performance. Source concludes 'In this letter' on p.8.
profiles.citation_profile: Bracket numeric baseline row labels; source citations are next to common perception/skeleton/partition modules. Numbered refs start p.8.

profiles.experiment_order: Training reward comparison -> global guidance/soft safety/hard filter ablation -> planner/learned baselines -> real speed x clutter -> outdoor and dynamic generalization (pp.5-7).
baseline_groups: Distance, Dijkstra, Dijkstra+CBF, full HOCBF shield; geometric inflation control (p.5).
Ego-Planner, NavRL, YOPO, DiffPhys; Ego-PlannerV2 for real comparison (pp.6-7).
metrics: Training success; task success with mean successful velocity; clearance; filter activation fraction; scene traversability; real successful velocity mean/std and dynamic success (pp.5-7).

profiles.transfer_boundary: Safety filter theory remains conditional on model/sensing assumptions; observed failures prevent unconditional physical safety claims. Native observations support system comparison, not isolated architecture superiority. Outdoor policy is not identical to original training setup.
profiles.citation_profile: Numeric IDs in baseline rows and figure captions; cited traversability metric and baseline implementation precede comparisons. Refs p.8.

profiles.experiment_order: Shared experimental protocol -> three task/scenes -> controlled geometric vs VLM selection across backbones -> capability coverage and targeted grounding/capability diagnostics (pp.5-7).

metrics: All-target success, successful-trial wall-clock time, per-robot/high-level total steps, reductions; qualitative task diagnostics (pp.6-7).
